subject: Food Science
title: The Birth of Breakfast Cereal
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Birth of Breakfast Cereal.

hook.text: Corn Flakes were invented by accident in 1894 when John Kellogg left cooked wheat sitting out, it went stale, and he rolled it.

buildup.text: Kellogg ran a sanitarium in Battle Creek, Michigan. He believed bland food cured illness and reduced 'sinful urges'.

discovery.text: His brother Will added sugar against John's wishes, marketed aggressively, and created the Kellogg Company.

twist.text: C.W. Post, a former Kellogg patient, stole the idea and launched Grape-Nuts (1897) and Post Toasties.

climax.text: Tony the Tiger (1952) and Toucan Sam (1963) turned cereal into children's entertainment.

punchline.text: Invented as bland health food. Became sugar-coated kids' snack.

quiz.question: What was John Kellogg's original purpose for creating cereal?
options: He believed bland food cured illness at his sanitarium—cereals were health foods
